scope.flow: RiskEngine.twapEMA() computes TWAP tick from OraclePack.getEMAs() and it is consumed by PanopticPool.getTWAP()/dispatchFrom() for staleness guards, solvency checks, and liquidation pricing
scope.environment: Solidity smart contract protocol (RiskEngine, OraclePack, PanopticPool)

statements.text: OraclePack.getEMAs() returns a tuple in the order spotEMA (index 0), fastEMA (index 1), slowEMA (index 2), eonsEMA (index 3), medianTick (index 4)
RiskEngine.twapEMA() unpacks the getEMAs() tuple in the wrong order
PanopticPool.getTWAP() consumes the incorrect TWAP tick and dispatchFrom() uses twapTick for liquidations/force exercises/settlements
Positional unpacking assigns eonsEMA <- spotEMA, slowEMA <- fastEMA, fastEMA <- slowEMA, so twapEMA() computes (6 * slow + 3 * fast + spot) / 10 instead of the intended 0.6*fast + 0.3*slow + 0.1*eons

The mathematically different TWAP can cause false positives/negatives in StaleOracle() checks, potentially allowing operations when the intended TWAP would block them, or blocking operations when the intended TWAP would allow them
Incorrect solvency classification at the TWAP checkpoint, since one of the four price points in the solvency grid is wrong
Incorrect liquidation bonus / conversion pricing inputs, since getLiquidationBonus is fed sqrtRatioAtTick(twapTick)
twapEMA() should compute the intended TWAP 0.6*fast + 0.3*slow + 0.1*eons, consistent with the system's own interpretation of getEMAs()

ambiguities: No attacker actor or unauthorized-caller condition is stated; the flaw is an internal computation error, not an access-control issue.
Report does not state a concrete observed transaction or numeric TWAP values; impacts are described as potential.
Whether the wrong TWAP actually triggers a specific liquidation or blocked operation is not demonstrated.
